title: Real-Time Identification of Fraud-Linked Cryptocurrency Exchanges from Victim-Reported Suspect Wallet Addresses through Automated Blockchain Analytics
department: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C),CIS Division
description:
• Background Cyber fraud victims increasingly report suspect cryptocurrency wallet addresses used by fraudsters for collection of funds in cases involving:
• investment scams,
• task-based frauds,
• sextortion,
• ransomware,
• phishing,
• darknet transactions,
• and organized cyber-enabled financial crimes.
During investigations, the reported wallet addresses are often:
• non-custodial wallets,
• temporary burner wallets,
• or intermediary wallets used for layering and laundering.
The inability to quickly identify the cryptocurrency exchange or VASP associated with these wallets delays:
• freezing of assets,
• preservation of evidence,
• tracing of fund flows,
• and victim fund recovery.
Manual blockchain tracing requires significant technical expertise and time, particularly in cases involving:
• multi-chain transfers,
• DeFi protocols,
• mixers/tumblers,
• bridges,
• and privacy-enhancing mechanisms.
• Description The proposed solution envisages a Real-Time Crypto Fraud Attribution System capable of automatically analyzing victim-reported wallet addresses and identifying the nearest exchange or VASP receiving direct deposits.
The system should:
• ingest wallet addresses reported through cybercrime complaint systems,
• automatically perform blockchain tracing,
• identify associated exchanges or VASPs,
• detect fund movement patterns,
• and generate actionable intelligence for investigators.
Key features may include:
• blockchain transaction graph analysis,
• clustering of exchange wallets,
• detection of intermediary laundering wallets,
• identification of cross-chain fund movement,
• integration with SAHYOG and NCRP platforms,
• automated alert generation,
• and risk categorization of wallets.
The system should support multiple blockchain ecosystems and provide:
• real-time tracing capability,
• automated investigative recommendations,
• and analytics dashboards for law enforcement agencies
• Expected Solution A software platform capable of:
• real-time blockchain intelligence generation,
• automated VASP identification,
• tracing of suspect wallets,
• cross-chain transaction analytics,
• fund-flow visualization,
• integration with LEA systems,
• and generation of standardized investigation reports.
The system should:
• reduce response time in cyber fraud investigations,
• improve freezing of proceeds of crime,
• enhance coordination with VASPs,
• and strengthen digital evidence collection capabilities.
The platform should further support:
• API integrations,
• scalable blockchain indexing,
• AI/ML-assisted risk detection,
• and automated pattern recognition for fraud typologies.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, blockchain applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on integration, api, blockchain. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 21/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: Real-Time Identification of Fraud-Linked Cryptocurrency Exchanges from Victim-Reported Suspect Wallet Addresses through Automated Blockchain Analytics

overview.in_plain_terms: When a fraud victim reports the crypto wallet address a scammer used, build a system that automatically and quickly figures out which real exchange the stolen money ended up at, so investigators can move fast to freeze it, before the trail goes cold.
overview.why_it_matters: In active fraud cases (investment scams, sextortion, phishing), the window to actually recover funds is short, once money reaches an exchange and gets cashed out or moved further, it's gone. Speed of attribution, right from the moment a victim reports a wallet, is the whole point here.
pain_points: Victims report a huge range of fraud types (investment scams, task-based frauds, sextortion, ransomware, phishing, darknet transactions), each potentially routing funds differently.
Reported wallets are often non-custodial, temporary burner wallets, or intermediary layering wallets, not the final destination.
Every delay in identifying the receiving exchange directly reduces the odds of freezing assets and recovering victim funds.
overview.background: Cyber fraud victims increasingly report suspect wallet addresses tied to a wide range of crimes. During investigation, reported wallets are typically non-custodial, burner, or intermediary wallets used for layering. Manual blockchain tracing to identify the associated exchange requires significant expertise and time, especially with multi-chain transfers, DeFi protocols, mixers, and bridges, all of which delay asset freezing, evidence preservation, and fund recovery.
overview.whats_being_asked: A Real-Time Crypto Fraud Attribution System that automatically analyzes victim-reported wallet addresses, performs blockchain tracing to identify the nearest exchange or VASP receiving direct deposits, detects fund-movement patterns, and generates actionable intelligence for investigators, supporting multiple blockchain ecosystems with real-time tracing and analytics dashboards.
expected_solution: Ingestion of victim-reported wallet addresses from cybercrime complaint systems.
Automated blockchain tracing to identify the nearest exchange or VASP receiving direct deposits.
Detection of fund-movement patterns and intermediary laundering wallets.
Cross-chain fund movement identification, and integration with SAHYOG and NCRP platforms.
Automated alert generation, wallet risk categorization, and analytics dashboards for law enforcement.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough band, edging above the closely related SIH26182 mainly on emphasis, this PS is framed explicitly around real-time, victim-report-triggered response speed, which pushes the design toward a genuinely time-critical pipeline rather than an offline investigative tool, that framing shift is the real innovation lever to lean into.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Same core technical challenge as the sibling PS (multi-chain tracing, cluster detection), plus the added requirement of doing it fast enough to matter for real-time fund-freezing decisions, which adds genuine engineering pressure around speed and automation.

competitive_landscape.note: As with SIH26182, this PS shares deep technical overlap with an adjacent I4C PS in the same batch, teams should pick one and build it with a clear, distinct emphasis, don't submit near-identical builds for both.

innovation.note: The real-time, victim-triggered response framing pushes this toward genuine time-critical system design, not just offline blockchain analytics.

invention.note: Multi-chain tracing plus a genuine speed/automation requirement (real-time, not batch) raises the engineering bar over a purely investigative tool.

technical_feasibility.note: As with the sibling PS, real commercial blockchain-intelligence tooling is paywalled, plan around free public block-explorer APIs and one primary blockchain for a genuinely working demo.

impact_and_benefits.note: Scored lower on impact than the sibling PS in the raw data, likely reflecting a narrower framing (attribution mechanics) versus the sibling's broader coordinated-response language, worth being aware of when pitching.

architecture.note: A genuinely real-time pipeline (ingest -> trace -> alert, fast) is architecturally more demanding than a batch/offline version of the same tracing logic.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Choose this over its sibling PS specifically if your team wants to build and demo the speed/automation angle, showing a trace complete in seconds after wallet submission, rather than just showing tracing capability exists. That live speed demo is your differentiator both from the sibling PS and from a generic blockchain-forensics pitch.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: The explicit 'real-time' framing gives you a concrete, measurable, demo-able metric (time from wallet submission to exchange identification) that most competing blockchain-tracing pitches won't showcase.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building essentially the same system as a team tackling the sibling SIH26182 PS, without a clear differentiated emphasis, risks both submissions looking redundant to judges evaluating both.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: if considering both this PS and SIH26182 as options, pick one, and if choosing this one, commit specifically to demonstrating and measuring real-time trace speed as your headline metric.

idea_0_4: Confirm this is your chosen PS (versus the closely related SIH26182) and commit to the real-time-speed framing as your differentiator.
Pick one blockchain for the fully-working demo (Ethereum recommended for free API support) and validate a real trace works against it immediately.
Assign owners: one on the tracing engine (optimized for speed), one on the real-time ingestion/alert pipeline, one on the investigator dashboard.
prototype_4_22: Build the wallet-submission-to-trace pipeline with a clock running, literally measure and log the time from input to identified exchange.
Build known-exchange hot-wallet address matching as your first-pass fast attribution method (real, publicly documented lists exist).
Add basic intermediary/layering-wallet hop-tracing for cases where the first hop isn't a known exchange.
integration_22_30: Wire the full real-time loop: wallet submitted -> automated trace -> exchange identified or escalated -> alert generated, with timing displayed.
Test against several real, publicly documented fraud-linked wallet addresses to validate both accuracy and speed.
Build the risk-categorization output (e.g. confidence level, number of hops, flagged intermediary types).
polish_30_36: Prepare a live demo: submit a wallet address on stage, watch the trace complete and the timer stop, with the identified exchange displayed.
Prepare a clear comparison framing: manual tracing takes hours/days of specialist time, this completes in seconds, with your actual measured number.
Be ready to explain honestly which blockchain(s) and fraud-wallet patterns are fully covered versus architecturally planned.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Put a visible stopwatch on the live demo, submit a wallet address and let judges watch the seconds tick by until the exchange is identified. That measured speed number, shown live, is a concrete, hard-to-fake proof point that most competing blockchain-tracing demos won't have.

strengths: The real-time framing gives a concrete, measurable, highly demo-able success metric.
Real public blockchain data means the demo is genuine, not simulated.
weaknesses: Significant technical overlap with the adjacent SIH26182 PS risks a confused or redundant pitch without deliberate differentiation.
True real-time performance at scale (versus a fast demo on one wallet) is a harder claim to fully substantiate in 36 hours.

roles_needed: Frontend developer (live dashboard with timing display)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: 2 blockchain/backend-focused to 1 frontend, speed and correctness of the tracing engine is what this PS's differentiation hinges on.
team_fit.approach: Instrument timing measurement into the pipeline from the very first prototype, not as an afterthought, since the real-time framing is your core differentiator, you need real numbers to show, not an estimate.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Block-explorer API integration, known-exchange address matching, and dashboard/timer UI can be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Deciding when to stop tracing (how many hops before declaring 'unresolved' rather than chasing an ever-longer chain) is a real design tradeoff between speed and completeness that needs deliberate human decision-making.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated tracing pipeline that was never actually benchmarked for speed, with a claimed 'real-time' capability that's just an unverified label, undermines the entire differentiator this PS is built around, measure and show real timing numbers.

data_resource_availability.status: Same as the sibling PS: free public block-explorer APIs (Etherscan, Blockchain.info) support real tracing; publicly documented fraud-linked wallet addresses exist from past incident writeups for realistic test cases.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If live API calls introduce latency that muddies your 'real-time' story, pre-cache the transaction graph data for your demo wallets so the live trace genuinely completes fast, and be transparent that production would need to handle live API latency at scale.

judge_qna.question: What does 'real-time' actually mean here, what's your measured latency?
judge_qna.strong_answer: For our tested wallet addresses, tracing completed in [X] seconds from submission to exchange identification, here's the measurement, and we're upfront that this used [live/cached] data.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would that latency change with a wallet that's been through 10+ intermediary hops instead of 1-2?

judge_qna.question: How do you decide when to stop tracing and declare a wallet 'unresolved'?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We set a hop-limit threshold based on typical fraud-layering patterns from public case studies, beyond that, we flag it for manual investigator review rather than claiming false certainty.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your hop-limit, and how did you arrive at that number?

judge_qna.question: This looks nearly identical to another PS in the set (SIH26182), why should we evaluate them as different solutions?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We deliberately built for measured real-time response speed as the primary success metric, versus a broader investigative-workflow framing, [explain the specific technical choices that reflect that emphasis].
judge_qna.follow_up: If both PS were merged into one production system, what would each contribute?
